## Keywords

{{< glossary screenplay scene scene-heading action-line dialogue subtext character-voice bark >}}

## 4.1 The screenplay format

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The animator, the voice actor and the programmer all read the same script.
- A scene heading gives INT. or EXT., the place and the time.
- Action lines show what we see and hear, and the dialogue stands under the character's name.
- **Do it:** In Script Formatter, tag the eight lines of the opening scene. Which line is the transition?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/script-page.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Parts of the page

a) Which part of the screenplay gives the place and the time of a scene?
b) What part is "(to herself)", under the name NOUR?
c) What is wrong with the action line "Nour remembers her father"?

::: {.answer}
a) the scene heading
b) a parenthetical
c) The camera cannot film a memory: write what we see, for example "Nour touches her father's old cap."
:::

## 4.2 What makes a scene

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A scene happens in one place and in one continuous time.
- A good scene has a goal, an obstacle and a turn at the end.
- A new place or a new time starts a new scene with a new heading.
- **Do it:** Write the heading, the goal, the obstacle and the turn of a cutscene you know.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/scene-parts.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · Scenes

a) Nour rows along the same street at the same time. Is it a new scene?
b) The boat reaches a rooftop at night. What must the script start?
c) Two characters greet each other, talk about the weather and leave. What is wrong with the scene?

::: {.answer}
a) No, it is still one scene.
b) a new scene with a new heading: EXT. ROOFTOP – NIGHT
c) Nothing changes in it.
:::

## 4.3 Dialogue that sounds like people

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Game dialogue is short, and each line does a job.
- Good dialogue shows a feeling instead of naming it: this is subtext.
- People never say "as you know" about things that both people know.
- **Do it:** In Dialogue Doctor, choose the better line in six pairs. How many stars do you get?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/dialogue-fix.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Fixing a line

The draft says: "I am very scared and very sad."
**How can the writer make this line better?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The line names the feelings, so the player has nothing to discover.
2. Real people often hide fear, so Nour can say that she is fine.
3. A better line is: **"I'm fine. Just… hold my hand."** The fear shows in the hand.
:::

## Live demo · Dialogue Doctor

{{< sim file="sims/dialogue-doctor.html" poster="sims/dialogue-doctor.png" title="Dialogue Doctor: choose the better line" task="**Show:** read both lines of each pair aloud and choose. **Ask:** which rule makes the better line better?" >}}

## Try it 3 · Better dialogue

a) What is wrong with "As you know, Nour, the river has flooded the whole city"?
b) What does the better line about holding a hand do well?
c) What is wrong with "Well, there are many ways, and some are better than others"?

::: {.answer}
a) Both characters already know it ("as you know").
b) It shows the fear with subtext.
c) It gives the player no goal.
:::

## 4.4 Barks

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A bark is a short line that plays during play when something happens.
- A table of barks gives each line its character and its trigger.
- The game plays a bark when its trigger happens.
- **Do it:** In Word or Excel, write three barks for a game you know, each with a trigger.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/line-table.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 4 · Barks

The facts: Nour's bark "Car ahead! Around it." plays when a floating car is in view. The family's bark "Over here! Please!" plays when the rooftop is in view.

a) Which line plays when a floating car comes into view?
b) Which column tells the programmer when a line plays?
c) Why must a bark be short?

::: {.answer}
a) "Car ahead! Around it."
b) the trigger
c) It can play many times in one level.
:::

## Game challenge · Rooftop Rescue

{{< sim file="sims/rooftop-rescue.html" poster="sims/rooftop-rescue.png" title="Rooftop Rescue: row, and watch each line play on its trigger" kind="game" task="**The story:** Nour rows down a flooded street to Grandma Salma's roof, and six lines play on their triggers. **Play:** row the boat, watch the table of barks, and choose Nour's answer at the roof." >}}

## Try it 5 · The next scene (harder)

The facts: the next scene of Rooftop Rescue happens on Salma's roof, at night. Salma will not leave her house.

a) Which heading fits the next scene?
b) Why does the next scene need a new heading?
c) Which action line can the camera film: "Salma holds the house key tight." or "Salma remembers her wedding day."?

::: {.answer}
a) EXT. ROOFTOP – NIGHT
b) The place and the time change.
c) "Salma holds the house key tight."
:::

## Summary

- A screenplay has a fixed format that the whole team can read.
- Action lines show only what we can see or hear.
- A scene has one place, one time, a goal, an obstacle and a turn.
- Good game dialogue is short and shows feelings with subtext.
- Barks play during play, each one on its trigger.
